terms.subject: Distributed Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: A collection of independent computers that appear to users as a single coherent system.
terms.simpleExplanation: Must handle partial failure, network delay, and consistency across nodes.

terms.subject: Distributed Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: A distributed system's ability to continue operating correctly despite component failures.
terms.simpleExplanation: Achieved through redundancy, replication, and failure detection mechanisms.

terms.subject: Distributed Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: Distributing incoming requests across multiple servers to optimize resource use and avoid overload.
terms.simpleExplanation: Improves availability and response time; common algorithms include round robin and least connections.

terms.subject: Generative AI
terms.simpleDefinition: A generative model that creates data by iteratively removing noise from a random starting point.
terms.simpleExplanation: The technique underlying most modern AI image generators.

terms.subject: Generative AI
terms.simpleDefinition: Further training a pre-trained model on a smaller, task-specific dataset.
terms.simpleExplanation: Adapts a general-purpose model to perform better on a specific domain or task.

terms.subject: Generative AI
terms.simpleDefinition: AI systems that create new content — text, images, audio, or code — rather than just classifying existing data.
terms.simpleExplanation: Powered largely by large language models and diffusion models.

terms.subject: Generative AI
terms.simpleDefinition: When a generative AI model produces confident but factually incorrect or fabricated output.
terms.simpleExplanation: A known limitation of large language models that users must watch for.

terms.subject: Generative AI
terms.simpleDefinition: A neural network trained on vast text data to understand and generate human-like language.
terms.simpleExplanation: Powers modern chatbots, coding assistants, and text generation tools.

terms.subject: Generative AI
terms.simpleDefinition: The practice of crafting inputs to guide a generative AI model toward a desired output.
terms.simpleExplanation: A key skill for effectively using large language models.

terms.subject: Git and Version Control
terms.simpleDefinition: An independent line of development within a repository.
terms.simpleExplanation: Lets developers work on features or fixes without affecting the main codebase.

terms.subject: Git and Version Control
terms.simpleDefinition: A snapshot of changes saved to a version control repository.
terms.simpleExplanation: Each commit records what changed, when, and by whom.

terms.subject: Git and Version Control
terms.simpleDefinition: Combining changes from one branch into another.
terms.simpleExplanation: Integrates independent lines of development back together.

terms.subject: Git and Version Control
terms.simpleDefinition: A situation where changes from two branches can't be automatically combined.
terms.simpleExplanation: Must be manually resolved by choosing or combining the conflicting changes.

terms.subject: Git and Version Control
terms.simpleDefinition: A request to merge changes from one branch into another, typically with review.
terms.simpleExplanation: The standard collaborative code-review workflow on platforms like GitHub.

terms.subject: Git and Version Control
terms.simpleDefinition: A storage location tracking a project's full history of changes.
terms.simpleExplanation: Can be local or hosted remotely on platforms like GitHub.

terms.subject: Human-Computer Interaction
terms.simpleDefinition: The study of how people interact with computers and how to design better interfaces.
terms.simpleExplanation: Combines psychology, design, and computer science.

terms.subject: Human-Computer Interaction
terms.simpleDefinition: How easily and effectively users can achieve their goals using a system.
terms.simpleExplanation: Measured through metrics like task success rate and time-on-task.

terms.subject: Human-Computer Interaction
terms.simpleDefinition: The overall experience a person has when interacting with a product or system.
terms.simpleExplanation: Encompasses usability, accessibility, and emotional response.

terms.subject: Human-Computer Interaction
terms.simpleDefinition: A low-fidelity visual layout outlining a screen's structure before visual design.
terms.simpleExplanation: Used early in design to focus on layout and flow rather than aesthetics.

terms.subject: Information Security
terms.simpleDefinition: Encryption using a public key to encrypt and a private key to decrypt.
terms.simpleExplanation: Solves the key-distribution problem of symmetric cryptography, at higher computational cost.

terms.subject: Information Security
terms.simpleDefinition: Verifying that a user or system is who it claims to be.
terms.simpleExplanation: Distinct from authorization, which determines what an authenticated identity is allowed to do.

terms.subject: Information Security
terms.simpleDefinition: A cryptographic mechanism verifying the authenticity and integrity of a message or document.
terms.simpleExplanation: Uses the sender's private key to sign and the public key to verify.

terms.subject: Information Security
terms.simpleDefinition: Transforming readable data into an unreadable form using a cryptographic key.
terms.simpleExplanation: Protects confidentiality; only someone with the correct key can decrypt it.

terms.subject: Information Security
terms.simpleDefinition: The practice of using firewalls and rule sets to control and monitor network traffic.
terms.simpleExplanation: A core layer of defense-in-depth network security.

terms.subject: Information Security
terms.simpleDefinition: Transforming data of any size into a fixed-size value (a hash), typically one-way.
terms.simpleExplanation: Used for data integrity checks, password storage, and hash tables.

terms.subject: Information Security
terms.simpleDefinition: Encryption using a mathematically linked key pair — one public, one private.
terms.simpleExplanation: Solves the problem of securely exchanging keys over an insecure channel.

terms.subject: Information Security
terms.simpleDefinition: An attack technique inserting malicious SQL through unsanitized user input.
terms.simpleExplanation: Prevented using parameterized queries and proper input validation.

terms.subject: Information Security
terms.simpleDefinition: Encryption where the same key is used for both encryption and decryption.
terms.simpleExplanation: Fast, but requires securely sharing the key between parties beforehand.

terms.subject: Internet of Things
terms.simpleDefinition: Processing data near where it's generated rather than sending it all to a central cloud.
terms.simpleExplanation: Reduces latency and bandwidth use for real-time IoT applications.

terms.subject: Internet of Things
terms.simpleDefinition: A physical object embedded with sensors and connectivity to exchange data over a network.
terms.simpleExplanation: Ranges from smart thermostats to industrial sensors.

terms.subject: Internet of Things
terms.simpleDefinition: A lightweight publish-subscribe messaging protocol designed for constrained IoT devices.
terms.simpleExplanation: Favored in IoT for its low bandwidth and power requirements.

terms.subject: Internet of Things
terms.simpleDefinition: A network of spatially distributed sensors monitoring physical or environmental conditions.
terms.simpleExplanation: Feeds real-world data into IoT and automation systems.

terms.subject: Java
terms.simpleDefinition: Platform-independent intermediate code produced by compiling Java source, executed by the JVM.
terms.simpleExplanation: Lets the same compiled file run on any system with a compatible JVM.

terms.subject: Java
terms.simpleDefinition: A mechanism for detecting and responding to runtime errors using try/catch blocks.
terms.simpleExplanation: Separates error-handling logic from normal program flow.

terms.subject: Java
terms.simpleDefinition: Automatic reclamation of memory occupied by objects no longer referenced by a program.
terms.simpleExplanation: Frees developers from manually tracking and releasing memory.

terms.subject: Java
terms.simpleDefinition: A packaged archive bundling compiled Java classes and resources for distribution.
terms.simpleExplanation: The standard format for distributing Java applications and libraries.

terms.subject: Java
terms.simpleDefinition: The runtime environment that executes compiled Java bytecode on any platform.
terms.simpleExplanation: Provides Java's 'write once, run anywhere' portability.

terms.subject: Java
terms.simpleDefinition: Running multiple threads concurrently within a single program.
terms.simpleExplanation: Improves responsiveness and throughput by overlapping independent tasks.

terms.subject: JavaScript
terms.simpleDefinition: Syntax that lets asynchronous, promise-based code be written in a synchronous-looking style.
terms.simpleExplanation: Makes asynchronous control flow easier to read and reason about.

terms.subject: JavaScript
terms.simpleDefinition: A function passed as an argument to be invoked after another operation completes.
terms.simpleExplanation: The foundational async pattern JavaScript originally relied on before promises.

terms.subject: JavaScript
terms.simpleDefinition: A function that retains access to its defining scope's variables even after that scope has exited.
terms.simpleExplanation: Enables data privacy and factory-function patterns in JavaScript.

terms.subject: JavaScript
terms.simpleDefinition: Document Object Model — a tree representation of an HTML page that JavaScript can read and modify.
terms.simpleExplanation: The interface through which scripts interact with web page content.

terms.subject: JavaScript
terms.simpleDefinition: The mechanism that lets JavaScript perform non-blocking I/O by handling callbacks after the current call stack clears.
terms.simpleExplanation: The reason JavaScript can be single-threaded yet handle many concurrent operations.

terms.subject: JavaScript
terms.simpleDefinition: An object representing the eventual result (or failure) of an asynchronous operation.
terms.simpleExplanation: Provides a cleaner alternative to nested callbacks for async code.

terms.subject: Machine Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: The algorithm that computes gradients to update a neural network's weights during training.
terms.simpleExplanation: Applies the chain rule of calculus layer by layer, from output back to input.

terms.subject: Machine Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: A technique for evaluating a model by training and testing on different data splits.
terms.simpleExplanation: Gives a more reliable estimate of how a model will perform on unseen data.

terms.subject: Machine Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: Selecting and transforming raw data into inputs that improve a model's predictive performance.
terms.simpleExplanation: Often has more impact on model quality than the choice of algorithm itself.

terms.subject: Machine Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: An optimization algorithm that iteratively adjusts parameters to minimize a loss function.
terms.simpleExplanation: Moves parameters in the direction that most reduces error, controlled by a learning rate.

terms.subject: Machine Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: A function measuring how far a model's predictions are from the true values.
terms.simpleExplanation: Training minimizes this function; common choices include cross-entropy and mean squared error.

terms.subject: Machine Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: A field of AI where systems learn patterns from data rather than being explicitly programmed.
terms.simpleExplanation: Encompasses supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning approaches.

terms.subject: Machine Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: A machine learning paradigm where an agent learns by receiving rewards or penalties for its actions.
terms.simpleExplanation: Used in game-playing AI, robotics, and sequential decision-making problems.

terms.subject: Machine Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: Machine learning where a model learns from labeled input-output pairs.
terms.simpleExplanation: Used for classification and regression tasks.

terms.subject: Machine Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: Machine learning that finds patterns or structure in unlabeled data.
terms.simpleExplanation: Used for clustering, dimensionality reduction, and anomaly detection.

terms.subject: Mobile Application Development
terms.simpleDefinition: Building apps that run on multiple platforms from a single shared codebase.
terms.simpleExplanation: Tools like React Native and Flutter trade some native performance for development speed.

terms.subject: Mobile Application Development
terms.simpleDefinition: A toolkit providing pre-built components for building mobile app interfaces.
terms.simpleExplanation: Speeds up development by providing consistent, reusable UI building blocks.

terms.subject: Mobile Application Development
terms.simpleDefinition: An application built specifically for one platform (iOS or Android) using its native tools.
terms.simpleExplanation: Offers the best performance and platform integration at the cost of duplicated effort.

terms.subject: Natural Language Processing
terms.simpleDefinition: Identifying and classifying named entities (people, places, organizations) in text.
terms.simpleExplanation: A core building block for information extraction systems.

terms.subject: Natural Language Processing
terms.simpleDefinition: The field enabling computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language.
terms.simpleExplanation: Powers translation, chatbots, sentiment analysis, and search engines.

terms.subject: Natural Language Processing
terms.simpleDefinition: Determining the emotional tone (positive, negative, neutral) expressed in text.
terms.simpleExplanation: Widely used to analyze reviews, social media, and customer feedback.

terms.subject: Natural Language Processing
terms.simpleDefinition: Splitting text into smaller units (words, subwords, or characters) for processing.
terms.simpleExplanation: The first preprocessing step in almost every NLP pipeline.

terms.subject: Natural Language Processing
terms.simpleDefinition: A neural network architecture using self-attention to process sequences in parallel.
terms.simpleExplanation: The foundation of modern large language models like GPT and BERT.

terms.subject: Natural Language Processing
terms.simpleDefinition: A dense vector representation of a word capturing its meaning based on context.
terms.simpleExplanation: Lets models compute semantic similarity between words mathematically.

terms.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A class that cannot be instantiated directly and may contain unimplemented methods.
terms.simpleExplanation: Serves as a base that concrete subclasses must complete.

terms.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: Hiding implementation details and exposing only essential features of an object.
terms.simpleExplanation: Lets programmers work with a simplified model rather than every internal detail.

terms.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A blueprint defining the properties and behaviors (methods) of its objects.
terms.simpleExplanation: Objects are instances created from a class.

terms.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A special method automatically invoked to initialize a newly created object.
terms.simpleExplanation: Sets an object's initial state when it's instantiated.

terms.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A special method automatically invoked when an object is destroyed, to release resources.
terms.simpleExplanation: Ensures cleanup like closing files or freeing memory.

terms.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: Bundling data and the methods that operate on it, restricting direct access to internal state.
terms.simpleExplanation: Protects an object's integrity by exposing only a controlled interface.

terms.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A mechanism where a class acquires properties and methods of another class.
terms.simpleExplanation: Promotes code reuse and models 'is-a' relationships between classes.

terms.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A contract specifying methods a class must implement, without providing the implementation.
terms.simpleExplanation: Lets unrelated classes share a common set of guaranteed behaviors.

terms.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: Defining multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists.
terms.simpleExplanation: Resolved at compile time based on the arguments provided.

terms.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A subclass providing its own implementation of a method already defined in its parent class.
terms.simpleExplanation: The basis of runtime polymorphism.

terms.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: An instance of a class, with its own state and access to class-defined behavior.
terms.simpleExplanation: Represents a concrete entity built from a class's blueprint.

terms.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: The ability of different classes to be treated through a common interface, each responding differently.
terms.simpleExplanation: Achieved via method overriding (runtime) or overloading (compile-time).

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: The OS mechanism for deciding execution order among ready processes.
terms.simpleExplanation: Balances throughput, turnaround time, waiting time, and response time.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: The CPU saving one process/thread's state and loading another's.
terms.simpleExplanation: Frequent context switching adds overhead, which is why the OS scheduler balances responsiveness against throughput.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: A code region accessing shared resources that must not be executed by more than one thread at once.
terms.simpleExplanation: Protected using mutexes, semaphores, or monitors to prevent race conditions.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: A state where two or more processes are permanently blocked, each waiting on a resource the other holds.
terms.simpleExplanation: Prevented via resource ordering, avoided via algorithms like Banker's, or resolved via detection and recovery.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: The OS structure organizing how data is stored, named, and retrieved on disk.
terms.simpleExplanation: Examples include NTFS, ext4, and FAT32.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: The core of an operating system, managing hardware, memory, and process scheduling.
terms.simpleExplanation: Runs in a privileged mode with direct hardware access.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: A locking mechanism ensuring only one thread accesses a critical section at a time.
terms.simpleExplanation: Unlike a semaphore, a mutex has ownership — only the thread that locked it can unlock it.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: System software that manages a computer's hardware and provides services for application programs.
terms.simpleExplanation: Handles process scheduling, memory management, file systems, and device I/O.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: An interrupt raised when a process accesses a page not currently in physical memory.
terms.simpleExplanation: The OS handles it by loading the page from disk, possibly evicting another page first.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: Dividing memory into fixed-size pages, mapped between virtual and physical addresses.
terms.simpleExplanation: Eliminates external fragmentation by allocating memory in uniform chunks.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: An instance of a program in execution, with its own memory space and resources.
terms.simpleExplanation: The OS scheduler allocates CPU time among competing processes.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: The OS activity of selecting which process runs on the CPU at any given moment.
terms.simpleExplanation: Balances fairness, throughput, and responsiveness using algorithms like Round Robin and Priority Scheduling.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: A bug where the outcome depends on the unpredictable timing of concurrent operations.
terms.simpleExplanation: Fixed by synchronizing access to shared data with locks or other primitives.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: The OS policy deciding which process/thread runs on the CPU next.
terms.simpleExplanation: Common algorithms include Round Robin, FCFS, SJF, and Priority Scheduling.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: Dividing a process's memory into variable-size logical segments (code, data, stack).
terms.simpleExplanation: Reflects a program's logical structure better than paging, at the cost of external fragmentation.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: A synchronization primitive using a counter to control access to a shared resource.
terms.simpleExplanation: Binary semaphores act like locks; counting semaphores limit access to N concurrent users.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: The interface through which user programs request services from the OS kernel.
terms.simpleExplanation: Examples include read, write, fork, and exec.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: A lightweight unit of execution within a process, sharing its memory space.
terms.simpleExplanation: Multiple threads let a program do work concurrently without the overhead of separate processes.

terms.subject: Operating Systems
terms.simpleDefinition: An abstraction giving each process the illusion of its own large, contiguous address space.
terms.simpleExplanation: Implemented via paging/segmentation, backed by physical RAM and disk.

terms.subject: Parallel Computing
terms.simpleDefinition: Computing performed by multiple independent computers coordinating over a network.
terms.simpleExplanation: Differs from parallel computing in that nodes don't share memory directly.

terms.subject: Parallel Computing
terms.simpleDefinition: The use of aggregated computing power (supercomputers, clusters) to solve large-scale problems.
terms.simpleExplanation: Used for simulations in weather forecasting, physics, and drug discovery.

terms.subject: Parallel Computing
terms.simpleDefinition: Message Passing Interface — a standard for communication between processes in parallel computing.
terms.simpleExplanation: The dominant programming model for distributed-memory HPC clusters.

terms.subject: Parallel Computing
terms.simpleDefinition: Performing multiple computations simultaneously by dividing a problem across multiple processors.
terms.simpleExplanation: Reduces total computation time for problems that can be broken into independent parts.

terms.subject: Parallel Computing
terms.simpleDefinition: Coordinating multiple threads' access to shared resources to prevent race conditions.
terms.simpleExplanation: Achieved using locks, semaphores, and other concurrency primitives.

terms.subject: Programming Fundamentals
terms.simpleDefinition: Exposing only essential features of an object while hiding implementation complexity.
terms.simpleExplanation: Lets programmers reason about a system at a higher, simpler level.

terms.subject: Programming Fundamentals
terms.simpleDefinition: A finite, well-defined sequence of steps that solves a problem or performs a computation.
terms.simpleExplanation: Every program is ultimately built from algorithms chosen for correctness and efficiency.

terms.subject: Programming Fundamentals
terms.simpleDefinition: Bundling an object's data with the methods operating on it, hiding internal state from outside access.
terms.simpleExplanation: Protects an object's integrity by controlling how its state can be changed.

terms.subject: Programming Fundamentals
terms.simpleDefinition: A mechanism letting a class acquire the properties and methods of another class.
terms.simpleExplanation: Promotes code reuse and models hierarchical relationships between types.

terms.subject: Programming Fundamentals
terms.simpleDefinition: A programming paradigm organizing code around objects that bundle data and behavior.
terms.simpleExplanation: Built on the pillars of encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.

terms.subject: Programming Fundamentals
terms.simpleDefinition: The ability for different object types to be used through a shared interface, each behaving differently.
terms.simpleExplanation: Lets code work generically with objects of related but distinct types.

terms.subject: Programming Fundamentals
terms.simpleDefinition: A function solving a problem by calling itself on smaller subproblems.
terms.simpleExplanation: Requires a base case to terminate; every recursive solution has an equivalent iterative one.

terms.subject: Programming Fundamentals
terms.simpleDefinition: In signal processing, an entity that transforms an input signal into an output signal.
terms.simpleExplanation: Characterized by properties like linearity, time-invariance, causality, and stability.

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A finite, step-by-step procedure for solving a problem.
terms.simpleExplanation: Before you can write a computer program, you first need a clear algorithm describing exactly what steps to follow.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A collection of values of the same type, stored together and accessed by a numeric index.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the fundamental way to store and work with a list of related data, like a set of exam scores.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A fast search method that repeatedly cuts a sorted list in half to zero in on the target value.
terms.simpleExplanation: It only works on sorted data, but it's dramatically faster than linear search for large lists.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A simple sorting algorithm that repeatedly swaps adjacent out-of-order elements until the list is sorted.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's easy to understand and implement, though not the fastest method for large lists.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A way of passing arguments to a function where the function can directly access and modify the original variable.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's used when a function actually needs to change the caller's original data, not just a copy.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A way of passing arguments to a function where the function receives a copy of the value, not the original.
terms.simpleExplanation: Changes made to the parameter inside the function don't affect the original variable outside it.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: An array of individual characters, commonly used to represent text (a string) in languages like C.
terms.simpleExplanation: In C, text is essentially just an array of characters ending with a special terminating character.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A program that translates source code written in a programming language into machine code the computer can execute.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the tool that turns your written C program into an actual runnable executable file.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: Choosing between different paths of execution in a program based on whether a condition is true or false.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's what lets a program make decisions, like an if-statement choosing between two possible actions.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A classification specifying what kind of value a variable can hold, such as an integer or character.
terms.simpleExplanation: The data type tells the compiler how much memory to use and what operations are valid on that data.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A complete, ready-to-run program file that the computer's operating system can directly execute.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the final product after source code has been compiled and linked.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: The set of operations a program uses to create, read, write, and close files stored on disk.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's how a program saves data permanently, beyond just what's held temporarily in memory while it runs.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A diagram using standard symbols to represent the steps and decision points of an algorithm.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's a visual way to plan a program's logic before writing any actual code.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A named, reusable block of code that performs a specific task and can be called from elsewhere in a program.
terms.simpleExplanation: Functions let you write a piece of logic once and reuse it, instead of repeating the same code everywhere.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A search method that checks each element of a list one by one until the target is found.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the simplest search strategy, though it can be slow for very large lists.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A data structure made of nodes, where each node holds data and a pointer to the next node.
terms.simpleExplanation: Unlike an array, a linked list can grow or shrink easily without needing a fixed block of memory upfront.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A mistake where a program runs without crashing but produces the wrong result.
terms.simpleExplanation: These are trickier than syntax errors because the program appears to work, just not correctly.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A programming structure that repeats a block of code multiple times.
terms.simpleExplanation: Loops let a program do repetitive tasks — like processing every item in a list — without duplicating code.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: The machine-readable output produced by a compiler from source code, not yet linked into a final executable.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's an intermediate step between human-written code and a finished, runnable program.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: The set of rules determining which operations in an expression are calculated first.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's why '2 + 3 * 4' equals 14, not 20 — multiplication is evaluated before addition.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A variable that stores the memory address of another variable, rather than a value itself.
terms.simpleExplanation: Pointers let a program work directly with memory locations, which is powerful but requires careful handling.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A program that processes source code before actual compilation, handling things like macro expansion and file inclusion.
terms.simpleExplanation: The #include and #define commands in a C program are handled by the preprocessor.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: An informal, plain-language way of describing an algorithm's logic without following a specific programming language's syntax.
terms.simpleExplanation: It lets you focus on the logic of a solution without worrying about exact syntax rules.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of the same problem.
terms.simpleExplanation: Recursion is a natural fit for problems that can be broken into smaller copies of themselves, like calculating a factorial.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A sorting algorithm that repeatedly finds the smallest remaining element and moves it into its correct position.
terms.simpleExplanation: It sorts by repeatedly selecting the best candidate from what's left, one position at a time.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A structure that contains a pointer to another instance of the same structure type.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the technique used to build data structures like linked lists, where each element points to the next.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: The human-readable instructions written by a programmer in a programming language.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's what you actually type when writing a program, before it's translated into something the computer can run.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A specifier in C that determines a variable's lifetime, visibility, and default value.
terms.simpleExplanation: Auto, static, register, and extern are the four storage classes that control how and where a variable is stored.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A user-defined data type that groups several related variables, possibly of different types, under one name.
terms.simpleExplanation: It lets you bundle related data together, like grouping a student's name, roll number, and marks into one unit.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A mistake that breaks the grammatical rules of a programming language.
terms.simpleExplanation: The compiler catches these before your program even runs, since it can't understand malformed code.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: An array arranged in rows and columns, like a grid or table.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the natural way to represent things like a matrix or a grid-based game board in code.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: The process of converting a value from one data type to another.
terms.simpleExplanation: It happens automatically in some cases, and explicitly (by the programmer) in others.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Programming for Problem Solving
terms.simpleDefinition: A named storage location in memory that holds a value which can change during a program's execution.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's how a program keeps track of and manipulates data as it runs.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Python
terms.simpleDefinition: A function that wraps another function to extend its behavior without modifying its code.
terms.simpleExplanation: Commonly used for logging, timing, and access control.

terms.subject: Python
terms.simpleDefinition: A function that yields values one at a time, pausing state between calls.
terms.simpleExplanation: Produces sequences lazily, saving memory for large or infinite sequences.

terms.subject: Python
terms.simpleDefinition: A mutex in CPython allowing only one thread to execute Python bytecode at a time.
terms.simpleExplanation: Limits true parallelism for CPU-bound multithreaded Python programs.

terms.subject: Python
terms.simpleDefinition: A program that executes source code line by line, without a separate compilation step.
terms.simpleExplanation: Python is interpreted (via CPython bytecode), trading raw speed for flexibility.

terms.subject: Python
terms.simpleDefinition: A concise syntax for constructing a new list by applying an expression to each item of an iterable.
terms.simpleExplanation: Reads close to natural language while being more efficient than an explicit loop.

terms.subject: Python
terms.simpleDefinition: An isolated Python environment with its own installed packages, separate from the system installation.
terms.simpleExplanation: Prevents dependency conflicts between different projects.

terms.subject: Quantum Computing
terms.simpleDefinition: A phenomenon where qubits become linked such that one's state instantly correlates with another's.
terms.simpleExplanation: A key resource exploited by quantum algorithms and quantum communication.

terms.subject: Quantum Computing
terms.simpleDefinition: An operation that manipulates the state of one or more qubits.
terms.simpleExplanation: The quantum analogue of a classical logic gate, building block of quantum circuits.

terms.subject: Quantum Computing
terms.simpleDefinition: The basic unit of quantum information, capable of existing in a superposition of 0 and 1.
terms.simpleExplanation: Unlike a classical bit, a qubit can represent multiple states simultaneously.

terms.subject: Quantum Computing
terms.simpleDefinition: A quantum property where a system exists in multiple states simultaneously until measured.
terms.simpleExplanation: Gives quantum computers their potential for massive parallelism.

terms.subject: Reinforcement Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: In reinforcement learning, the decision-maker that interacts with an environment.
terms.simpleExplanation: Learns a policy mapping states to actions that maximizes cumulative reward.

terms.subject: Reinforcement Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: A strategy mapping states to actions that an agent follows.
terms.simpleExplanation: The reinforcement learning agent's ultimate learned output.

terms.subject: Reinforcement Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: A model-free reinforcement learning algorithm that learns the value of action-state pairs.
terms.simpleExplanation: One of the foundational algorithms in reinforcement learning.

terms.subject: Reinforcement Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: A machine learning paradigm where an agent learns by taking actions and receiving rewards or penalties.
terms.simpleExplanation: Used in game-playing AI, robotics, and autonomous decision-making systems.

terms.subject: Reinforcement Learning
terms.simpleDefinition: A function defining the feedback signal an agent receives for its actions.
terms.simpleExplanation: Shapes what behavior the agent learns to optimize for.

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: Extremely large or complex datasets that traditional data-processing methods struggle to handle.
terms.simpleExplanation: Specialized tools and techniques are needed to store, process, and extract insight from big data.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A numerical method for finding a function's root by repeatedly halving an interval known to contain it.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's a simple, reliable, if somewhat slow, way to numerically solve equations by computer.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: The graphical representation of data to make patterns and insights easier to understand.
terms.simpleExplanation: Tools like Matplotlib and MATLAB's plotting functions turn raw numbers into interpretable charts.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A Python collection that stores data as key-value pairs for fast lookup by key.
terms.simpleExplanation: Instead of finding an item by its position like in a list, you look it up directly by its key.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A network of physical devices embedded with sensors and software that connect and exchange data over the internet.
terms.simpleExplanation: Smart home devices and industrial sensors are everyday examples of IoT.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: An ordered, changeable collection of items in Python.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's Python's flexible, general-purpose way of storing a sequence of values.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A programming environment specialized for numerical computing, matrix operations, and engineering simulations.
terms.simpleExplanation: Its name literally stands for 'Matrix Laboratory', reflecting its origins in linear algebra computation.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A field of computing where systems learn patterns from data rather than being explicitly programmed with rules.
terms.simpleExplanation: The Scientific Programming course introduces it as one of several emerging technologies students should be aware of.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A popular Python library used for creating charts and graphs.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the standard tool Python programmers reach for to visualize data.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A mathematical operation — like addition, multiplication, or inversion — performed on matrices.
terms.simpleExplanation: MATLAB was specifically designed to make these operations fast and easy to write.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A numerical method for finding a function's root using the function's slope to converge quickly on an answer.
terms.simpleExplanation: It typically converges much faster than the bisection method, though it needs a good starting guess.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: The process of approximating the value of an integral using numerical computation rather than an exact formula.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's essential when a function is too complex to integrate by hand, or is only known from data points.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: A widely used, beginner-friendly programming language known for readable syntax.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's one of the two languages (with MATLAB) the Scientific Programming course uses for numerical and data work.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Scientific Programming
terms.simpleDefinition: An ordered, unchangeable collection of items in Python.
terms.simpleExplanation: Unlike a list, once created, a tuple's contents can't be modified.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A defined interface letting different software components communicate with each other.
terms.simpleExplanation: Lets developers use functionality without needing to know its internal implementation.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: An iterative software development approach emphasizing short cycles and adapting to change.
terms.simpleExplanation: Delivers working software in small increments (sprints) with continuous feedback.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The practice of having other developers examine code changes before they're merged.
terms.simpleExplanation: Catches bugs, improves code quality, and spreads knowledge across a team.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: Automatically releasing every change that passes tests into production.
terms.simpleExplanation: Extends continuous integration all the way to live users.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A practice of frequently merging code changes into a shared repository with automated builds and tests.
terms.simpleExplanation: Catches integration issues early, before they compound.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A general, reusable solution to a commonly occurring software design problem.
terms.simpleExplanation: Examples include Singleton, Factory, Observer, and Strategy.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: An architectural style structuring an application as a collection of small, independently deployable services.
terms.simpleExplanation: Trades the simplicity of a monolith for independent scalability and deployment.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: An architectural style where an entire application is built and deployed as a single unit.
terms.simpleExplanation: Simpler to develop initially but harder to scale and update piecemeal.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The software engineering phase of gathering and specifying what a system must do.
terms.simpleExplanation: Produces requirement documents that guide design and testing.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The high-level structure of a software system — its components and how they interact.
terms.simpleExplanation: Determines a system's scalability, maintainability, and performance characteristics.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The structured process of planning, designing, building, testing, and maintaining software.
terms.simpleExplanation: Common models include Waterfall, Agile, and Spiral.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The process of evaluating software to find defects and verify it meets requirements.
terms.simpleExplanation: Includes unit, integration, system, and acceptance testing.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The process of defining a system's architecture, components, and interfaces to satisfy requirements.
terms.simpleExplanation: Central to building software that can scale and evolve over time.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The implied future cost of choosing an easy, short-term solution over a better long-term one.
terms.simpleExplanation: Left unaddressed, it accumulates and slows future development.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: Testing individual components or functions of software in isolation.
terms.simpleExplanation: Catches bugs early and enables safe refactoring.

terms.subject: Software Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A system that tracks changes to source code over time, enabling collaboration and rollback.
terms.simpleExplanation: Git is the dominant distributed version control system today.

terms.subject: Theory of Computation
terms.simpleDefinition: A grammar where each production rule has a single non-terminal on its left side.
terms.simpleExplanation: Used to define the syntax of most programming languages.

terms.subject: Theory of Computation
terms.simpleDefinition: Whether an algorithm exists that always halts with a correct yes/no answer for a problem.
terms.simpleExplanation: The halting problem is the classic example of an undecidable problem.

terms.subject: Theory of Computation
terms.simpleDefinition: An abstract machine with a finite number of states used to recognize patterns.
terms.simpleExplanation: Regular expressions and finite automata are equivalent in what they can recognize.

terms.subject: Theory of Computation
terms.simpleDefinition: A class of decision problems believed to have no known polynomial-time solution.
terms.simpleExplanation: If any NP-complete problem is solved in polynomial time, all of NP can be.

terms.subject: Theory of Computation
terms.simpleDefinition: An automaton with a stack, recognizing context-free languages.
terms.simpleExplanation: More powerful than a finite automaton because of its unbounded stack memory.

terms.subject: Theory of Computation
terms.simpleDefinition: A pattern describing a set of strings, used for matching and searching text.
terms.simpleExplanation: Powers lexical analysis, text search, and input validation.

terms.subject: Theory of Computation
terms.simpleDefinition: A theoretical computing model with an infinite tape, defining the limits of computability.
terms.simpleExplanation: Used to formally define what problems are algorithmically solvable.

terms.subject: TypeScript
terms.simpleDefinition: A way to write components that work with a variety of types while preserving type safety.
terms.simpleExplanation: Avoids duplicating code for each specific type while keeping type checking.

terms.subject: TypeScript
terms.simpleDefinition: A TypeScript construct defining the shape an object must conform to.
terms.simpleExplanation: Enforced only at compile time, with no runtime footprint.

terms.subject: TypeScript
terms.simpleDefinition: Explicitly specifying a variable's or function's expected type.
terms.simpleExplanation: Improves tooling support and catches type mismatches before runtime.

terms.subject: TypeScript
terms.simpleDefinition: A compiler's ability to automatically deduce a variable's type from its usage.
terms.simpleExplanation: Lets TypeScript catch type errors without requiring every type to be written explicitly.

terms.subject: Web Development
terms.simpleDefinition: Building the server-side logic, databases, and APIs behind a web application.
terms.simpleExplanation: Handles business logic, data storage, and security.

terms.subject: Web Development
terms.simpleDefinition: Cascading Style Sheets — the language used to style and lay out HTML content.
terms.simpleExplanation: Controls a web page's colors, fonts, spacing, and responsive layout.

terms.subject: Web Development
terms.simpleDefinition: An architecture where client devices request services from a centralized server.
terms.simpleExplanation: The foundational model underlying almost all web applications.

terms.subject: Web Development
terms.simpleDefinition: Building the user-facing part of a web application that runs in the browser.
terms.simpleExplanation: Focuses on layout, interactivity, and user experience.

terms.subject: Web Development
terms.simpleDefinition: Working across both the frontend and backend of a web application.
terms.simpleExplanation: Requires familiarity with client-side, server-side, and database technologies.

terms.subject: Web Development
terms.simpleDefinition: HyperText Markup Language — the standard language for structuring content on the web.
terms.simpleExplanation: Defines a page's elements like headings, paragraphs, links, and images.

terms.subject: Web Development
terms.simpleDefinition: Designing web pages to render well across different screen sizes and devices.
terms.simpleExplanation: Achieved with flexible layouts, relative units, and media queries.

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A machine that generates alternating current, typically driven by a rotating mechanical source.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the modern generator type used in power plants and vehicles to produce AC electricity.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The product of RMS voltage and RMS current in an AC circuit, combining real and reactive power.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's what a power supply must actually be rated to handle, even though not all of it does useful work.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The distorting effect that current in a machine's armature winding has on its main magnetic field.
terms.simpleExplanation: It affects the performance and voltage regulation of both DC and AC electrical machines.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A transformer with a single winding shared between the primary and secondary circuits.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's more compact and efficient than a standard transformer but doesn't electrically isolate the two sides.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The voltage a motor generates that opposes the supply voltage driving it, due to it also acting like a generator while spinning.
terms.simpleExplanation: It naturally limits a motor's current draw once it's up to speed.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A property of a circuit element that stores electrical energy in an electric field between two conductive surfaces.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the defining property of a capacitor, determining how much charge it can hold at a given voltage.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A circuit component that stores electrical energy in an electric field between two plates.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's used to store charge, filter signals, and smooth out voltage fluctuations in circuits.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A single-phase induction motor that uses a capacitor to create the extra phase shift needed to start turning.
terms.simpleExplanation: Single-phase motors can't self-start without this trick, unlike three-phase motors.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The rate of flow of electric charge through a conductor.
terms.simpleExplanation: Measured in amperes; determined by voltage and resistance via Ohm's Law.

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A machine that converts mechanical energy into direct-current electrical energy.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the historical predecessor to the AC alternators used in most modern power generation.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A three-phase circuit connection where the windings are connected end-to-end in a closed triangle loop.
terms.simpleExplanation: Unlike a star connection, a delta connection has no neutral point.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: Earth Leakage Circuit Breaker — a safety device that disconnects power when it detects current leaking to earth.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's a key safety feature that protects people from electric shock in household wiring.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The formula relating a generator's induced voltage to its speed, magnetic flux, and winding design.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the design equation engineers use to predict how much voltage a generator will produce.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: Connecting the metal body of electrical equipment to the ground to prevent dangerous voltage buildup.
terms.simpleExplanation: It gives fault current a safe path to flow through instead of through a person who touches the equipment.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The generation of a voltage in a conductor caused by a changing magnetic field.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the fundamental principle behind how generators and transformers produce electricity.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The induced voltage in a circuit equals the rate of change of magnetic flux through it.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the mathematical rule that quantifies electromagnetic induction.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The total opposition an AC circuit offers to current flow, combining resistance and reactance.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the AC equivalent of resistance, but it also accounts for the effects of capacitors and inductors.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A property of a circuit element that opposes changes in current by storing energy in a magnetic field.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's what makes a coil (inductor) resist sudden changes in the current flowing through it.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A circuit component, usually a coil of wire, that stores energy in a magnetic field when current flows through it.
terms.simpleExplanation: It resists sudden changes in current, unlike a plain resistor.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The total current flowing into a junction in a circuit equals the total current flowing out.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's a bookkeeping rule: charge can't pile up or vanish at a junction, so what goes in must come out.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The sum of all voltage changes around any closed loop in a circuit equals zero.
terms.simpleExplanation: It reflects that energy gained and lost around a complete loop in a circuit must balance out.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The direction of an induced current always opposes the change that created it.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's nature's way of resisting change — think of it as electromagnetic 'inertia'.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: Miniature Circuit Breaker — a resettable switch that automatically trips to cut power during an overload or short circuit.
terms.simpleExplanation: Unlike a fuse, an MCB can simply be reset and reused after it trips.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: Any complex two-terminal linear circuit can be replaced by a single current source in parallel with a single resistor.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the current-source counterpart to Thevenin's theorem, useful in different circuit-analysis situations.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: States that voltage equals current times resistance (V = IR) in a conductor.
terms.simpleExplanation: The fundamental relationship underlying almost all circuit analysis.

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A rotating vector representation used to simplify calculations with sinusoidal AC quantities.
terms.simpleExplanation: It turns messy trigonometric AC math into simpler vector addition and rotation.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The ratio of real (usable) power to apparent (total) power in an AC circuit.
terms.simpleExplanation: A low power factor means a lot of power is being drawn but not usefully converted to work.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The effective value of an alternating current or voltage, equivalent to the steady DC value that would deliver the same power.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's why household AC voltage is rated by its RMS value, not its peak value.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: Power that oscillates back and forth in an AC circuit without doing any real work.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's associated with energy storage in inductors and capacitors rather than being consumed.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The actual power consumed and converted into useful work in an AC circuit.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the power that actually does work, like lighting a bulb or turning a motor.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A material's opposition to the flow of electric current.
terms.simpleExplanation: Measured in ohms; converts electrical energy to heat as current flows through it.

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A basic circuit component that opposes the flow of electric current, converting electrical energy into heat.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's one of the three fundamental passive circuit elements, alongside capacitors and inductors.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: The difference between the rotating magnetic field's speed and the actual rotor speed in an induction motor, expressed as a fraction.
terms.simpleExplanation: An induction motor can only produce torque when there's some slip — it can never spin at exactly the field's speed.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A simple, rugged induction-motor rotor made of conducting bars short-circuited at both ends, resembling a rotating cage.
terms.simpleExplanation: Its simplicity and durability make it the most common rotor type in industrial motors.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: A three-phase circuit connection where one end of each phase winding is joined at a common neutral point.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's one of the two standard ways (with delta) to wire three-phase electrical systems.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: In a circuit with multiple sources, the effect of each source can be calculated separately and then added together.
terms.simpleExplanation: It lets you simplify a complicated circuit by analyzing one source at a time.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Basic Electrical Engineering
terms.simpleDefinition: An electrical protection device combining a switch and a fuse to safely isolate a circuit.
terms.simpleExplanation: It provides a manual way to disconnect a circuit along with automatic protection against overcurrent.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)
