terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: A function that extends the factorial to non-integer and complex numbers.
terms.simpleExplanation: It lets you make sense of something like '3.5 factorial', which ordinary factorial can't define.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: A multiplier applied to a differential equation to make it exact and therefore solvable.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's a trick for turning an otherwise unsolvable-looking equation into one you can integrate directly.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: The process of converting a Laplace-transformed expression back into its original time-domain function.
terms.simpleExplanation: After solving the easier algebraic version of a problem, this step translates the answer back to something meaningful in time.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: A tool that converts a differential equation in time into an algebraic equation in a new variable, making it easier to solve.
terms.simpleExplanation: Engineers use it to turn hard calculus problems (like circuit or control-system equations) into simple algebra.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: A family of special polynomials that are solutions to Legendre's differential equation.
terms.simpleExplanation: They're widely used to describe potentials and fields around spherical objects in physics and engineering.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: A specific differential equation whose polynomial solutions (Legendre polynomials) appear throughout physics and engineering.
terms.simpleExplanation: Its solutions describe things like the shape of gravitational or electric potentials around spherical objects.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: A differential equation where the unknown function and its derivatives appear only to the first power, with no products between them.
terms.simpleExplanation: Its 'linear' structure makes it far more tractable than general differential equations.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: A set of vectors is linearly independent if none of them can be written as a combination of the others.
terms.simpleExplanation: If vectors are dependent, one is redundant — it points in a direction already covered by the rest.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: A function between vector spaces that preserves addition and scalar multiplication.
terms.simpleExplanation: Rotations, scalings, and reflections are all linear transformations — they can all be represented by a matrix.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: A technique for solving non-homogeneous differential equations by letting constants become functions.
terms.simpleExplanation: It works even when simpler guess-and-check methods fail.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: A curve that crosses every member of a given family of curves at a right angle.
terms.simpleExplanation: Field lines and equipotential lines in physics are classic orthogonal trajectories of each other.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: A linear transformation that preserves lengths and angles.
terms.simpleExplanation: Rotations and reflections are orthogonal transformations — they move vectors around without stretching or distorting them.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: An expression built from squared and cross-product terms of variables, using a matrix to organize the coefficients.
terms.simpleExplanation: Quadratic forms show up when studying curves and surfaces like ellipses and conics in higher dimensions.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: The number of independent rows (or columns) a matrix has.
terms.simpleExplanation: It tells you how much genuinely new information the matrix's rows carry, which decides whether a system of equations has a unique solution.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: A specific type of nonlinear first-order differential equation with a characteristic squared term.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's a well-studied nonlinear equation type with known substitution techniques for certain solvable cases.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Differential Equations & Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: A compact formula for generating Legendre polynomials directly through repeated differentiation.
terms.simpleExplanation: It gives a systematic shortcut for writing down any Legendre polynomial without solving the differential equation each time.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Graph Theory (Mathematics)
terms.simpleDefinition: A connection between two vertices in a graph.
terms.simpleExplanation: May be directed or undirected, weighted or unweighted.

terms.subject: Graph Theory (Mathematics)
terms.simpleDefinition: A subgraph connecting all vertices of a graph with the minimum number of edges and no cycles.
terms.simpleExplanation: A minimum spanning tree connects all vertices at the lowest total edge weight.

terms.subject: Graph Theory (Mathematics)
terms.simpleDefinition: A fundamental unit (node) of a graph, representing an entity.
terms.simpleExplanation: Connected to other vertices via edges to form the graph's structure.

terms.subject: Linear Algebra
terms.simpleDefinition: A scalar value computed from a square matrix, indicating properties like invertibility.
terms.simpleExplanation: A zero determinant means the matrix is singular (non-invertible).

terms.subject: Linear Algebra
terms.simpleDefinition: A rectangular array of numbers arranged in rows and columns.
terms.simpleExplanation: Used to represent and solve systems of linear equations, and to describe linear transformations.

terms.subject: Linear Algebra
terms.simpleDefinition: A collection of vectors closed under addition and scalar multiplication.
terms.simpleExplanation: The foundational structure underlying linear algebra.

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: When a series converges even after making every term positive.
terms.simpleExplanation: Absolute convergence is a stronger, more robust form of convergence than merely converging with the signs left in.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A series whose terms alternate between positive and negative.
terms.simpleExplanation: Because the signs flip, alternating series can converge even when the series of their absolute values doesn't.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A generalization of Lagrange's theorem comparing the rates of change of two functions at once.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the tool behind proving certain limit rules like L'Hopital's rule.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A convergence test based on taking the nth root of the nth term of a series.
terms.simpleExplanation: Like the ratio test, it gives a quick way to check convergence, useful when terms involve powers.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: The circle that best matches a curve's bend at a given point.
terms.simpleExplanation: It shares the same curvature, tangent direction, and position as the curve at that exact point.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A convergence test that checks a series against another series already known to converge or diverge.
terms.simpleExplanation: If your series' terms are always smaller than a series you know converges, yours converges too.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: When a series converges only because of the alternating signs, not on its own.
terms.simpleExplanation: Remove the minus signs and a conditionally convergent series would actually diverge.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A rule used to decide whether an infinite series adds up to a finite value.
terms.simpleExplanation: Since you can't literally add infinitely many numbers by hand, convergence tests give a shortcut to decide if the sum settles down.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A measure of how much a vector field rotates or swirls around a point.
terms.simpleExplanation: It captures the local spinning tendency of a field, like the tendency of water to form a whirlpool.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A convergence test that looks at the ratio of consecutive terms of a series.
terms.simpleExplanation: If that ratio settles below 1, the series converges; above 1, it diverges — named after mathematician Jean le Rond d'Alembert.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: The rate at which a function changes as you move in a specific chosen direction.
terms.simpleExplanation: It generalizes the ordinary derivative to any direction, not just along the x or y axis.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A measure of how much a vector field spreads out from (or converges into) a point.
terms.simpleExplanation: Positive divergence at a point means the field acts like a source there; negative means a sink.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: An integral that adds up a function's values over a two-dimensional region.
terms.simpleExplanation: Where a single integral finds area under a curve, a double integral finds volume under a surface.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: The curve traced by the centers of curvature of another curve.
terms.simpleExplanation: As you slide along a curve, its evolute is the path swept out by the center of the best-fit circle at each point.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A theorem relating the flow of a vector field out of a closed surface to the divergence inside it.
terms.simpleExplanation: It connects what happens on a surface to what happens throughout the volume it encloses.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A vector that points in the direction a function increases fastest, with a magnitude equal to that rate.
terms.simpleExplanation: Walking in the gradient direction gets you uphill fastest on a surface described by the function.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A theorem relating a line integral around a closed curve to a double integral over the region it encloses.
terms.simpleExplanation: It lets you trade a boundary calculation for an area calculation, whichever is easier.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A curve traced by unwinding a taut string from another curve.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the reverse relationship of an evolute — gears often use involute curves for smooth, constant-speed meshing.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A matrix (or its determinant) of all first-order partial derivatives of a set of functions.
terms.simpleExplanation: It measures how a transformation stretches or shrinks area/volume when changing variables, e.g. from Cartesian to polar coordinates.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: For a smooth curve between two points, some point on the curve has a slope equal to the average slope between the endpoints.
terms.simpleExplanation: It guarantees that somewhere along the way, your instantaneous rate of change matches your overall average rate of change.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A technique for finding the maximum or minimum of a function subject to a constraint.
terms.simpleExplanation: Instead of solving the constraint directly, you introduce an extra variable (multiplier) that ties the function and constraint together.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: The rate of change of a multivariable function with respect to just one variable, holding the others fixed.
terms.simpleExplanation: It tells you how steep a surface is if you only walk in one particular direction.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A finer convergence test used when the ratio test is inconclusive (ratio equals 1).
terms.simpleExplanation: It looks more closely at how fast the ratio approaches 1 to settle cases the ratio test can't decide.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A number describing how sharply a curve bends at a point.
terms.simpleExplanation: A small radius of curvature means a sharp bend; a large one means the curve is almost straight.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: If a smooth curve starts and ends at the same height, it must be flat (zero slope) somewhere in between.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the geometric intuition behind why a ball thrown up and caught at the same height must, at some instant, stop rising.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: An ordered, unending list of numbers formed by some rule, the basic building block for studying series.
terms.simpleExplanation: In Math-I you study whether a sequence settles down to one number (converges) or keeps growing/oscillating (diverges).
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: The sum of the terms of a sequence, one after another.
terms.simpleExplanation: Adding up infinitely many terms of a sequence gives a series, and a central question is whether that infinite sum is a finite number.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A theorem relating the circulation of a vector field around a closed loop to the curl over the surface it bounds.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the higher-dimensional cousin of Green's theorem, used heavily in electromagnetism.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: A way to approximate a function near a point using a polynomial built from its derivatives.
terms.simpleExplanation: It lets you replace a complicated function with a simpler polynomial that behaves almost the same nearby.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: An expression for the total change in a multivariable function caused by small changes in all its variables at once.
terms.simpleExplanation: It combines all the partial derivatives to estimate the overall change, not just change along one axis.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: An integral that adds up a function's values over a three-dimensional region.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's used to compute quantities like mass or volume that depend on all three spatial directions.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Matrices & Differential Calculus
terms.simpleDefinition: The branch of calculus dealing with vector fields — quantities with both magnitude and direction that vary in space.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the mathematical language used to describe things like fluid flow, electric fields, and gravity.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: Approximating derivatives by using differences between function values at nearby points.
terms.simpleExplanation: A common technique for numerically solving differential equations.

terms.subject: Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: Estimating unknown values that fall between known data points.
terms.simpleExplanation: Widely used to approximate a function from a limited set of sampled data.

terms.subject: Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: An iterative numerical technique for finding roots of a real-valued function.
terms.simpleExplanation: Converges quickly when the initial guess is reasonably close to the true root.

terms.subject: Numerical Methods
terms.simpleDefinition: Approximating the value of a definite integral using numerical techniques rather than an exact formula.
terms.simpleExplanation: Necessary when a function has no closed-form antiderivative.

terms.subject: Optimization
terms.simpleDefinition: A restriction limiting the feasible values a solution to an optimization problem can take.
terms.simpleExplanation: Defines the boundaries of the feasible region an optimal solution must lie within.

terms.subject: Optimization
terms.simpleDefinition: A method for optimizing a linear objective function subject to linear constraints.
terms.simpleExplanation: Widely used for resource allocation, scheduling, and logistics problems.

terms.subject: Optimization
terms.simpleDefinition: The function an optimization problem seeks to maximize or minimize.
terms.simpleExplanation: Defines what 'better' means for a given optimization problem.

terms.subject: Probability and Statistics
terms.simpleDefinition: A statistical method for deciding whether evidence supports or contradicts an assumption about data.
terms.simpleExplanation: Used across science and engineering to validate findings with quantified confidence.

terms.subject: Probability and Statistics
terms.simpleDefinition: A function describing the likelihood of different outcomes of a random variable.
terms.simpleExplanation: Common examples include normal, binomial, and Poisson distributions.

terms.subject: Probability and Statistics
terms.simpleDefinition: A statistical technique for modeling the relationship between a dependent variable and one or more predictors.
terms.simpleExplanation: Widely used for prediction and understanding relationships between variables.

terms.subject: Probability and Statistics
terms.simpleDefinition: A measure of how spread out data values are from their mean.
terms.simpleExplanation: A small standard deviation means data points cluster tightly around the average.

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The maximum angle at which light can enter an optical fiber and still be guided by total internal reflection.
terms.simpleExplanation: Light entering steeper than this angle escapes the fiber instead of traveling down it.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A theory explaining superconductivity through electrons pairing up (Cooper pairs) via lattice vibrations.
terms.simpleExplanation: Named after Bardeen, Cooper, and Schrieffer, it was the first successful microscopic explanation of superconductivity.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A ferroelectric ceramic material widely used in capacitors and sensors.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's one of the most common examples used to illustrate ferroelectric behavior in engineering physics.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The equation describing the exact condition under which X-rays reflected from crystal planes reinforce each other.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the foundation of X-ray diffraction, the main technique for determining crystal structures.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: One of the 14 distinct ways points can be arranged periodically in 3D space to form a crystal structure.
terms.simpleExplanation: Every real crystal's atomic arrangement can be described using one of these fundamental repeating patterns.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A vector that measures the size and direction of the lattice distortion caused by a dislocation.
terms.simpleExplanation: It quantifies exactly how much a crystal's structure is 'off' around a dislocation line.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The number of charge carriers (electrons or holes) per unit volume in a material.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's a key factor determining how well a semiconductor conducts electricity.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A measure of how resistant a magnetic material is to becoming demagnetized.
terms.simpleExplanation: High coercivity materials make good permanent magnets since they resist losing their magnetism.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: One of a handful of standard geometric categories a crystal's repeating structure can belong to (e.g. cubic).
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the basic classification scheme used to describe how a crystal's building block repeats in space.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The scientific study of how atoms are arranged in a crystal.
terms.simpleExplanation: Understanding this arrangement explains why crystals have the shapes, strengths, and electrical properties they do.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The wavelength associated with any moving particle, linking its momentum to wave-like behavior.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the key idea behind wave-particle duality — even matter has a wavelength, though usually too small to notice.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A material that weakly repels an external magnetic field.
terms.simpleExplanation: All materials show some diamagnetism, though it's usually masked by stronger magnetic effects if present.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A material that does not conduct electricity but can be polarized by an electric field.
terms.simpleExplanation: Capacitors use dielectrics between their plates to store more electrical energy.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A line-shaped defect in a crystal where the regular atomic arrangement is disrupted along a line.
terms.simpleExplanation: Dislocations are central to understanding how metals bend and deform without breaking.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A term Maxwell added to account for changing electric fields acting like a current, even with no actual charge flow.
terms.simpleExplanation: It was the missing piece needed to make Maxwell's equations consistent and to predict electromagnetic waves.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A range of allowed electron energy levels in a solid, separated from other bands by forbidden gaps.
terms.simpleExplanation: Whether a material is a conductor, insulator, or semiconductor depends on how these bands are filled and spaced.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A semiconductor deliberately doped with impurity atoms to boost its conductivity.
terms.simpleExplanation: Almost all real semiconductor devices use extrinsic, not intrinsic, semiconductor material.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A ceramic magnetic material combining iron oxide with other metal oxides, useful because it's magnetic but electrically insulating.
terms.simpleExplanation: Its insulating nature makes it ideal for high-frequency transformer cores where ordinary metal cores would lose energy.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A property where a material retains electrical polarization even after the external field is removed.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the electrical analogue of ferromagnetism, used in some sensors and memory devices.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A material that can be strongly and permanently magnetized.
terms.simpleExplanation: Iron, nickel, and cobalt are classic ferromagnetic materials used in magnets and transformers.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A simplified model treating the electrons in a metal as a gas of free particles, ignoring the atomic lattice's details.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's a first approximation that explains basic metallic properties like electrical conductivity.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A crystal defect where an atom leaves its normal site and wedges into a gap elsewhere in the lattice.
terms.simpleExplanation: Unlike a Schottky defect, the displaced atom isn't lost — it's just relocated to an unusual position.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The appearance of a sideways voltage across a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's used to measure magnetic fields and to determine whether a semiconductor's carriers are electrons or holes.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A magnetic material that resists demagnetization and retains its magnetism strongly.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the type of material used to make permanent magnets.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A gas laser using a mixture of helium and neon to produce a red laser beam.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's one of the most common and inexpensive lasers, often used for alignment and barcode scanning.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A missing electron in a semiconductor's bonding structure that behaves like a positive charge carrier.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's a bookkeeping trick: instead of tracking billions of electrons, you track the few 'holes' they leave behind.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The lag between a material's magnetization and the applied magnetic field, causing energy loss over a cycle.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's why transformer cores heat up slightly — some energy is lost each time the field reverses direction.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The distance between adjacent parallel planes of atoms in a crystal.
terms.simpleExplanation: It directly determines how X-rays diffract off the crystal, which is how crystal structures are measured experimentally.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A pure semiconductor with no added impurities, where conductivity comes only from thermally generated charge carriers.
terms.simpleExplanation: Silicon in its pure form is a classic intrinsic semiconductor.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A quantum model showing how electrons behave in a periodic potential like that of a crystal lattice.
terms.simpleExplanation: It explains why electron energies in solids form 'bands' rather than being spread continuously.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A device that produces a highly focused, single-color, coherent beam of light through stimulated emission.
terms.simpleExplanation: Its name is literally an acronym: Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: Four equations that together fully describe classical electricity, magnetism, and their interaction.
terms.simpleExplanation: They predict that changing electric and magnetic fields propagate as electromagnetic waves — including light.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The expulsion of magnetic field from the interior of a superconductor.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the signature phenomenon that makes superconductors levitate above magnets.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A set of three numbers used to label the orientation of a plane within a crystal.
terms.simpleExplanation: They give crystallographers a compact shorthand for referring to any particular slice through a crystal's structure.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A number describing how much light an optical fiber (or lens) can accept and still guide properly.
terms.simpleExplanation: A higher numerical aperture means the fiber can collect light from a wider range of angles.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A thin strand of glass or plastic that carries light signals over long distances by total internal reflection.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the backbone of modern high-speed internet and telecommunications.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A semiconductor device formed where p-type and n-type material meet, allowing current to flow mainly in one direction.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the fundamental building block behind rectifiers, LEDs, and most semiconductor electronics.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A simplified quantum model of a particle confined to a region with impenetrable walls.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the simplest example used to show how quantum confinement leads to discrete, quantized energy levels.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A localized imperfection in a crystal involving just one or a few atomic sites.
terms.simpleExplanation: Even a 'perfect' crystal has some of these naturally, and they strongly affect properties like conductivity and strength.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The slight separation of positive and negative charge within a material's atoms or molecules under an electric field.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's what allows an insulating material to still respond to and store energy from an electric field.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A state where more atoms are in a higher energy level than a lower one — the opposite of normal.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the essential condition that must be created inside a laser for it to amplify light.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A technique for studying crystal structure using a powdered (not single-crystal) sample and X-rays.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's widely used because powders are much easier to prepare than perfect single crystals.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A theorem describing the flow of energy carried by an electromagnetic field.
terms.simpleExplanation: It tells you the direction and rate at which electromagnetic energy — like from a light wave — actually moves through space.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A measure of how much magnetism a material retains after an external magnetic field is removed.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's what determines how 'permanent' a magnet stays after it's been magnetized.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A solid-state laser using a ruby crystal as its light-amplifying medium.
terms.simpleExplanation: It was the first working laser ever built, in 1960.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A crystal defect where an atom is missing entirely from its normal lattice site.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's essentially a vacancy — an empty spot where an atom should be.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The fundamental equation governing how a quantum system's wave function evolves over time.
terms.simpleExplanation: It plays the same central role in quantum mechanics that Newton's laws play in classical mechanics.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A compact laser that generates light directly from a semiconductor material, similar to an LED.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the type of laser found inside everyday devices like laser pointers and optical disc drives.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A magnetic material that is easily magnetized and demagnetized, with low hysteresis loss.
terms.simpleExplanation: Transformer cores use soft magnetic materials so they can be rapidly re-magnetized each AC cycle with little energy loss.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The process where an incoming photon triggers an excited atom to emit an identical photon.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the core mechanism that makes laser light coherent and amplifiable, as opposed to ordinary spontaneous light emission.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A state where a material conducts electricity with exactly zero resistance below a critical temperature.
terms.simpleExplanation: It allows current to flow forever with no energy loss, unlike ordinary conductors.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A resistor whose resistance changes significantly and predictably with temperature.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's commonly used as a simple, accurate temperature sensor.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A superconductor that abruptly and completely expels magnetic fields below its critical temperature.
terms.simpleExplanation: It behaves in the simplest, most 'textbook' way among superconducting materials.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A superconductor that allows partial magnetic field penetration in a mixed state before fully expelling it.
terms.simpleExplanation: Most practical, high-field superconducting magnets are made from Type II materials.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A mathematical function in quantum mechanics that encodes everything knowable about a particle's state.
terms.simpleExplanation: Its square gives the probability of finding the particle at a given place — quantum mechanics deals in probabilities, not certainties.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics Lab
terms.simpleDefinition: A number describing how much a material can store electrical energy compared to a vacuum.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's measured experimentally in the physics lab to characterize materials like PZT.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics Lab
terms.simpleDefinition: A measure of a solar cell's efficiency, comparing its actual maximum power output to its theoretical maximum.
terms.simpleExplanation: A higher fill factor means the solar cell is closer to performing at its ideal potential.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics Lab
terms.simpleDefinition: A graph showing the lag between a material's magnetization and the applied magnetic field over a full cycle.
terms.simpleExplanation: Its enclosed area represents the energy lost as heat during one magnetization cycle.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics Lab
terms.simpleDefinition: A graph showing how the current through a device varies with the voltage applied across it.
terms.simpleExplanation: Plotting a diode's I-V curve in the lab reveals its distinctive one-way conduction behavior.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Engineering Physics Lab
terms.simpleDefinition: An experimental setup used to measure a material's rigidity by observing its twisting oscillations.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's a classic physics-lab method for determining the modulus of rigidity of a wire or rod.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Nanotechnology
terms.simpleDefinition: A material with structural features at the nanometer scale, often exhibiting unique properties.
terms.simpleExplanation: Properties can differ dramatically from the same material at bulk scale.

terms.subject: Nanotechnology
terms.simpleDefinition: A particle with dimensions between roughly 1 and 100 nanometers.
terms.simpleExplanation: Used in applications from drug delivery to advanced electronics.

terms.subject: Optics
terms.simpleDefinition: The combination of two or more light waves resulting in a new wave pattern.
terms.simpleExplanation: Produces phenomena like the colors seen in soap bubbles and thin films.

terms.subject: Optics
terms.simpleDefinition: The bending of light as it passes between media of different densities.
terms.simpleExplanation: The principle behind lenses, prisms, and fiber-optic communication.

terms.subject: Quantum Mechanics
terms.simpleDefinition: States certain pairs of physical properties (like position and momentum) can't both be precisely known simultaneously.
terms.simpleExplanation: A fundamental limit of nature, not a limitation of measurement technology.

terms.subject: Quantum Mechanics
terms.simpleDefinition: The concept that particles like electrons and photons exhibit both wave-like and particle-like behavior.
terms.simpleExplanation: A foundational, counterintuitive principle of quantum mechanics.

terms.subject: Semiconductor Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: Intentionally introducing impurities into a semiconductor to modify its electrical properties.
terms.simpleExplanation: Creates n-type or p-type semiconductors, the building blocks of diodes and transistors.

terms.subject: Semiconductor Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The boundary between p-type and n-type semiconductor material within a single crystal.
terms.simpleExplanation: The fundamental structure enabling diodes, transistors, and solar cells.

terms.subject: Semiconductor Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: A material with electrical conductivity between that of a conductor and an insulator.
terms.simpleExplanation: Its conductivity can be precisely controlled via doping, the basis of modern electronics.

terms.subject: Solid State Physics
terms.simpleDefinition: The regular, repeating arrangement of atoms in a crystalline solid.
terms.simpleExplanation: Determines many of a material's electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties.

terms.subject: Air Pollution Control
terms.simpleDefinition: A substance in the air that can harm human health or the environment.
terms.simpleExplanation: Includes particulate matter, sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, and carbon monoxide.

terms.subject: Air Pollution Control
terms.simpleDefinition: A standardized measure communicating how polluted the air currently is.
terms.simpleExplanation: Translates pollutant concentrations into an easily understood public health scale.

terms.subject: Air Pollution Control
terms.simpleDefinition: A device that removes pollutants from industrial exhaust gases before release.
terms.simpleExplanation: Commonly used to remove sulfur dioxide and particulates from smokestacks.

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: Rainfall made abnormally acidic by pollutants like sulfur and nitrogen oxides in the atmosphere.
terms.simpleExplanation: It can damage forests, acidify lakes, and corrode buildings and monuments.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: The contamination of air by substances harmful to health or the environment.
terms.simpleExplanation: Vehicle emissions and industrial smoke are among the biggest contributors to air pollution.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: The variety of life — species, genes, and ecosystems — found in a particular area or on Earth as a whole.
terms.simpleExplanation: High biodiversity generally makes an ecosystem more resilient to disturbance and change.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: An organism that obtains energy by eating other organisms rather than producing its own food.
terms.simpleExplanation: Consumers are classified by what they eat — herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat other animals.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: An organism that breaks down dead organic matter, recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.
terms.simpleExplanation: Without decomposers like fungi and bacteria, nutrients would stay locked up in dead material forever.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: The organized process of preparing for, responding to, and recovering from natural or man-made disasters.
terms.simpleExplanation: It covers everything from early warning systems to post-disaster relief and rebuilding.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: A diagram showing the relative amount of energy, biomass, or numbers of organisms at each feeding level of an ecosystem.
terms.simpleExplanation: It typically narrows toward the top, showing how much energy is lost at each step of a food chain.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: The gradual, predictable process by which an ecosystem's species composition changes over time.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's how a bare patch of land can slowly transform into a mature forest over decades.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: A community of living organisms interacting with each other and their physical environment.
terms.simpleExplanation: A pond, a forest, and even a puddle can each be studied as a self-contained ecosystem.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: A species at serious risk of becoming extinct in the near future.
terms.simpleExplanation: Conservation programs specifically target endangered species to prevent their extinction.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: A species found naturally only in one specific geographic area and nowhere else.
terms.simpleExplanation: Endemic species are often especially vulnerable since their entire population is concentrated in one place.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: A sequence showing who eats whom, tracing the transfer of energy from one organism to the next.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the simplest way to visualize how energy moves through an ecosystem, from producer to top predator.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: The long-term rise in Earth's average surface temperature, largely driven by human greenhouse gas emissions.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's the underlying cause behind broader climate change effects like melting ice caps and rising sea levels.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: An energy source that exists in a limited supply and cannot be replenished within a human lifetime.
terms.simpleExplanation: Coal, oil, and natural gas are the classic examples — once used, they're effectively gone for good.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: The thinning of the ozone layer in the upper atmosphere, historically caused mainly by certain industrial chemicals.
terms.simpleExplanation: A thinner ozone layer lets more harmful ultraviolet radiation reach Earth's surface.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: An organism, typically a plant, that makes its own food using sunlight through photosynthesis.
terms.simpleExplanation: Producers form the base of every food chain — nearly all other life ultimately depends on them.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: An energy source that naturally replenishes and won't run out on human timescales, like solar or wind.
terms.simpleExplanation: Shifting toward renewable resources reduces dependence on finite fossil fuels.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: The contamination of soil with harmful chemicals or waste that degrades its quality.
terms.simpleExplanation: It can make land unsuitable for agriculture and can also contaminate groundwater over time.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: The systematic process of collecting, treating, and disposing of solid waste materials.
terms.simpleExplanation: It's essential for preventing pollution and disease in growing towns and cities.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Environmental Sciences
terms.simpleDefinition: The contamination of water bodies, making them harmful to health or ecosystems.
terms.simpleExplanation: Industrial discharge and untreated sewage are common causes of water pollution.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: Solid Waste Management
terms.simpleDefinition: The controlled biological decomposition of organic waste into nutrient-rich material.
terms.simpleExplanation: Diverts organic waste from landfills while producing useful soil amendment.

terms.subject: Solid Waste Management
terms.simpleDefinition: An engineered site for the disposal of solid waste by burial.
terms.simpleExplanation: Modern landfills use liners and monitoring to prevent groundwater contamination.

terms.subject: Solid Waste Management
terms.simpleDefinition: Processing used materials into new products to reduce waste and raw material use.
terms.simpleExplanation: Reduces the volume of waste sent to landfills and conserves natural resources.

terms.subject: Sustainability
terms.simpleDefinition: The total greenhouse gas emissions caused by an individual, organization, or product.
terms.simpleExplanation: Used to quantify and target reductions in contribution to climate change.

terms.subject: Sustainability
terms.simpleDefinition: Evaluating a product's environmental impact across its entire life, from raw material to disposal.
terms.simpleExplanation: Helps identify the most impactful stages to target for improvement.

terms.subject: Sustainability
terms.simpleDefinition: Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet their own.
terms.simpleExplanation: A guiding principle across modern engineering design and policy.

terms.subject: Water Treatment
terms.simpleDefinition: Adding chemicals to water to clump together suspended particles for easier removal.
terms.simpleExplanation: A key early step in conventional water treatment before filtration.

terms.subject: Water Treatment
terms.simpleDefinition: Treating water to kill or inactivate harmful microorganisms, commonly with chlorine or UV light.
terms.simpleExplanation: The final safeguard ensuring water is safe to drink.

terms.subject: Water Treatment
terms.simpleDefinition: The application of engineering to protect and improve environmental quality.
terms.simpleExplanation: Covers water/wastewater treatment, air quality, and waste management.

terms.subject: Water Treatment
terms.simpleDefinition: Passing water through a porous medium to remove suspended solids and impurities.
terms.simpleExplanation: A core physical treatment step in both water and wastewater treatment.

terms.subject: English
terms.simpleDefinition: A sentence structure where the subject performs the action described by the verb.
terms.simpleExplanation: 'The dog chased the ball' is in active voice — the subject (dog) does the action.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: English
terms.simpleDefinition: A word that means the opposite of another word.
terms.simpleExplanation: 'Hot' and 'cold' are antonyms.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: English
terms.simpleDefinition: Reporting someone's exact words, usually within quotation marks.
terms.simpleExplanation: 'She said, "I am tired"' is direct speech — it quotes the exact original words.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: English
terms.simpleDefinition: A word that shares the same spelling or sound as another word but has a different meaning.
terms.simpleExplanation: 'Bank' (a riverbank) and 'bank' (a financial institution) are homonyms.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: English
terms.simpleDefinition: A word that sounds the same as another word but has a different meaning and often a different spelling.
terms.simpleExplanation: 'Their', 'there', and 'they're' are classic homophones that trip up even fluent speakers.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: English
terms.simpleDefinition: Reporting what someone said without quoting their exact words.
terms.simpleExplanation: 'She said that she was tired' is indirect speech — it paraphrases rather than quotes.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: English
terms.simpleDefinition: A sentence structure where the subject receives the action instead of performing it.
terms.simpleExplanation: 'The ball was chased by the dog' is the same idea in passive voice.
terms.source: OU Faculty of Engineering, AICTE Model Curriculum first-year B.E. syllabus (2020-24 batch, mirrored via MVSR Engineering College) cross-checked against the official OU 2024-25 (R24) first-year syllabus PDFs (osmania.ac.in)

terms.subject: English
terms.simpleDefinition: A group of letters added to the beginning of a word to change its meaning.
terms.simpleExplanation: Adding 'un-' to 'happy' to form 'unhappy' is a classic example of a prefix at work.
